# Helium — calculated thermodynamic functions

<!-- generated-by: sync-thermochemistry.mjs -->

Source: SRC-000509, NIST Chemistry WebBook / Chase (1998), retrieved 2026-10-05. These are calculations from dated fits, not new measurements. Values below are rounded to four decimal places for computational comparison; this is not a statement of physical precision. Uncertainty: UNKNOWN. Basis: **mol He**.

[Full calculation and limits](../0002-Helium-He-Thermochemistry.md) · [Complete 101-point-per-fit CSV](0002-Helium-He-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) · [Exact coefficients](../data/structured/0002-Helium-He-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml)

| Fit | Variant | T / K | Cp° / J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | S° / J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | H°(T)−H°(298.15 K) / kJ mol⁻¹ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 298.0000 | 20.7860 | 126.1415 | -0.0031 |
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 3149.0000 | 20.7860 | 175.1497 | 59.2579 |
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 6000.0000 | 20.7860 | 188.5500 | 118.5188 |

Each row uses only the named phase and fit interval. Do not subtract rows from different phases to obtain transition enthalpy without first resolving their standard-state reference offsets.

sources.scope_note: A dated 5 October 2026 gas-thermochemistry retrieval of the existing NIST Helium work. Its retained thermal page and comparison table are a source revision/scope link, not independent corroborating evidence. Existing source metadata are unchanged.
sources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook — neutral monatomic Helium gas thermochemistry (5 October 2026 retrieval)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.scope: Neutral monatomic He only, not He2, an excimer, He ions, atomic nuclei or an equilibrium mixture. No molecular factor of two applies. Source formula He and molecular weight do not establish numeric He-3/He-4 abundances or isotope-specific thermal properties. Existing He-3/He-4 branches and statistics retain separate scope. Only GAS298–6000K fit is supplied. No extrapolation to cryogenic helium, isotope-specific phase behaviour, liquid/solid states, lambda points, superfluidity or superconductivity is justified. The fit equations supply standard thermochemical functions without a pressure variable. No arbitrary-pressure EOS, applied sample pressure or pressure-temperature phase diagram is inferred. Any separate reference-pressure label belongs to its own datum. Do not import Hydrogen ortho/para assumptions into monatomic Helium or assign a spin mixture. Isotope nuclear-spin distinctions do not turn this elemental gas fit into isotope-specific models. Coefficient uncertainty and covariance are unreported. Publisher rounding and numerical derivative residuals are source-format/software checks, not physical uncertainty. Transcription arithmetic and positive within-fit samples do not establish independent calorimetry, replication, complete Helium thermophysics or scientific completion.
sources.reference: Chase, M.W., Jr. (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition. Fit comment: Data last reviewed in March, 1982.
